questionsToConsider: How many initial concepts will you present, and should the ending say so?
Do you want a budget question, or do you quote after reading the brief?
Which file formats will you deliver, and does the client need to know now?
Should the personality words be your own vocabulary rather than these?
guide.howToUseResponses: Read the brief before the kickoff call and list anything that conflicts, such as premium and playful together, so you can ask about it directly. Build a moodboard from the uploaded references and the notes on what the client likes. Keep the usage answers in front of you while designing, because a logo that must work as an app icon or embroidered on a shirt needs to survive at small sizes and in one colour.
customizeSteps: Swap the personality words for the vocabulary you already use with clients.
Add your process to the ending, such as how many rounds of revisions are included.
Send the link as soon as a client signs, or embed it on your enquiry page so the brief arrives with the lead.

faqs.q: What should a logo design brief include?
faqs.a: The business name, what it does, who its customers are, the feel it wants, examples it likes and every place the logo will be used. Deadlines and existing brand colours help too.

faqs.q: Why ask where the logo will be used?
faqs.a: A logo that works on a website may fail as a tiny app icon or in one colour on packaging. Knowing the uses early shapes the design.

faqs.q: Should I ask clients for reference logos?
faqs.a: Yes. References are faster than descriptions, and asking what they like about each one tells you more than the images alone.

faqs.q: Can I use this form for a full brand identity project?
faqs.a: Yes. Copy it with Use this template and add questions about typography, tone of voice or brand guidelines.
